# Vendored front-end libraries

Served from Coral's own origin (`/static/vendor/`); the dashboard CSP allows scripts from `'self'` only.
Generated by `tests/frontend/vendor_manifest.mjs --write`; `node tests/frontend/vendor_manifest.mjs` (in `npm run test:cloud`)
fails if a file or this table drifts, and `--fetch` re-derives every row from the npm registry.
To update a library: replace the file, set its version and tarball sha256 in the script, run `--fetch`, then `--write`.
The fonts are listed in `fonts/README.md`.

## `codemirror/codemirror-bundle.js`

SHA-256 `7f76b559e3c98a67e47f0c601856c1bb85f25025ab443e836d7997325da37295`. An esbuild 0.28.1 IIFE (window.CoralCM) of CodeMirror 6 and its @lezer parsers, built from the input in `tests/vendor-build/codemirror` (package.json with exact versions, package-lock.json, entry.js). Byte-verified: `node vendor_manifest.mjs --rebuild` runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` there and `esbuild entry.js --bundle --format=iife --global-name=CoralCM --minify`, and the output must equal this file. The lock was resolved with `npm install --before=2026-03-23T18:06:23Z`, the date of the earlier build, whose output this file replaces: the two have the same size and differ in 8 bytes, all minified variable names (the lang-sql dialect tables and yaml-frontmatter); the earlier build's input was never recorded, so that difference is not traced to a package. (codemirror by its latest tag: 6.65.7 is an old CodeMirror 5 publish.) esbuild was raised from 0.27.4 to 0.28.1 (#5545, the npm audit finding) with the same output: the rebuild is byte for byte this file under both.

## `safe-markdown.js` (shared with Coral Hub)

SHA-256 `f2e534847b953ab44c4f832e753ff9caf632bb93db9e8b56fbb9be82e79b1fad`, pinned in `tests/frontend/vendor_manifest.mjs`. From Coral Hub, internal/accountui/assets/markdown.js (AccountMarkdown). A small DOM-built markdown renderer for machine-supplied text (the shared Inbox, #5754): no HTML sink, no images, only http, https and mailto links with the host shown, hidden characters stripped, bounded work. A classic script, loaded on first use by vendor_loader.js (loadSafeMarkdown, #5818: not by the page); safe_markdown.js is its ES wrapper. Byte-identical to the hub's copy: the hub pins the same hash.

The hub pins the same hash. A change to this file needs Security on both sides. `tests/frontend/fixtures/markdown-corpus.mjs` (pinned by the same test, `4365c0455bd41e4dc013ffda0f5ac5b5fb9d2c21fc9515d02132678d62e0def3`) is the hostile-input corpus both repos run against it in a real browser.

## Update rule for DOMPurify and marked

They sanitize and render the agent-written HTML and markdown of the chat, the board, the docs and the artifact viewer. A security advisory for either one means an update of that file: within 7 days when it is rated high or critical, within 30 days otherwise. 
Before the new version lands the whole front-end suite runs on it, with `html_interpolation_census` and `fixtures/markdown-corpus.mjs` (the shared hostile corpus) in a real browser. The Inbox does not use them (it uses `safe-markdown.js`).

## Notes

- `purify.min.js`: Sanitizes all agent-written HTML. Also byte-identical to dist/purify.min.js at the GitHub tag 3.4.17.
- `xterm/addon-canvas.min.js`: Upstream deprecates it in later xterm lines; pinned, revisit at the next xterm bump.
